summary: Kevin Buckelew specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College, with doctoral supervisors Chun-fang Yu, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang, committee member T. Griffith Foulk, and teachers Yan Ling, Fumiko Nazikian, and Courtney Bender.
Khakyab Dorje (1871–1922) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1885–1892) and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thayé (~1886–1899), and he taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Khammai Dhammasami is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford (~1999–2004). He served as a fellow and trustee at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (~2004) and as a professor at ITBMU (attested 2013).
Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk (1938–2014) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued traditional studies under Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Lodro Gyatso.

Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (1933–2023) studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (~1959–1981) in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He founded Thrangu Monastery, served as abbot of Rumtek Monastery (~1976), and became director of the Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (~1981).

Khenpo Appey (1927–2010) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dzongsar Monastery (1950) and under Khenpo Dragyab Lodrö. He held a post at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and served as head and director of Sakya College.

Khenpo Dazer studied under Bötrül Dongak Tenpé Nyima in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He taught at Dzogchen Monastery and Ngagyur Nyingma Institute, and his students include Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche.

Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (1924–2019) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Thrangu Monastery (~1936–1958), later teaching at Rumtek Monastery (1959) and serving as abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra (1978).
Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He undertook traditional studies under Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.

Khenpo Palden Sherab (1938–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Gochen and Riwoche Monasteries. He served as chair of the Nyingma section at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche (1920–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Dudjom Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and others. He founded Nyingmapa Wishfulfilling Center (1971) and taught at Tokyo, Kyoto, and Virginia universities.

Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (1895–1977) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Rumtek Monastery and under Khenpo Shenga, Rasvir Das, Dev Narayan Tripathi, and Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, later teaching at Men-Tsee-Khang.
Ki-yong Rhi (1922–1996) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was affiliated with Dongguk University (attested 1983), where he later served as professor emeritus (attested 2007).
Kichinosuke Ito (1885–1961) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Chuo University, Hokkaido University, and served as a professor at the University of Tokyo.
Kim Gutschow works in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University and has taught at Wesleyan University.
Kim Knott is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She held posts at the University of Leeds (~1986–2012) and Lancaster University (~2012).

Kim Plofker specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Haverford College and Brown University under David Pingree, and held positions at MIT, the American Oriental Society, and Union College (2007).

Kimberley C. Patton is a religious studies scholar who completed her dissertation at Harvard University (~1985–1992). She was an associate at the ASCSA (1991) and served as assistant professor in religion at Harvard (~1990).

Kimiaki Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ratnakaji Bajracharya, holding posts at the University of Tokyo, Eastern Institute, Toho Gakuin, and Keio University.

Kimmo Koskenniemi is a linguist who studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu. At the University of Helsinki, he served as Professor of Computer Linguistics (~1989–2013) and director of the BAULT research community (attested 2015).
